introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examinations. Food and Nutrition 2 (0540), ORDINARY LEVEL, June 2025. Duration: two and a half hours.**

Instructions to candidates: ANSWER ANY FOUR QUESTIONS.

You are reminded of the necessity of good English and orderly presentation of work. Tabulate wherever possible and use diagrams where appropriate.

Points : chaque question imprime « Total = 25 marks » et les points imprimés des sous-questions totalisent bien 25 pour chacune des 6 questions (aucun écart). Quand une sous-question (a), (b), (c) ou (d) porte des parties (i) et (ii), `points` de la sous-question est la somme des parties imprimées.

Question 2(e) : T.V.P. est complété par « Textured Vegetable Protein » et H.B.V. par « High Biological Value » (protein), valeurs usuelles d'un cours de nutrition ; le sujet ne précise pas qu'il s'agit de protéines pour H.B.V. Le sujet imprime « as used in nutrition.; » (ponctuation recopiée telle quelle).

Faits de cours à relire par un enseignant de Food and Nutrition : les règles d'hygiène personnelle (2a), les agents de contamination (2b), les moyens d'économiser le gaz (2c) et les épices (2d). Le sujet n'impose aucune liste ; aucune donnée chiffrée n'est avancée.

questions.enonce_markdown:
State five (5) personal hygiene rules.

(5 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Five personal hygiene rules for a person who prepares food (1 mark each):

1. **Wash the hands** with soap and clean water before handling food, after using the toilet and after touching the hair, nose or refuse.
2. **Tie up or cover the hair** with a cap or a hair net.
3. **Wear a clean apron** and clean clothes, and bathe daily.
4. **Keep the nails short and clean**, and take off rings and watches.
5. **Cover cuts and sores** with a waterproof dressing, and do not cough or sneeze over food or taste food with the fingers.

questions.enonce_markdown:
List five (5) agents of food contamination.

(5 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Five agents of food contamination (1 mark each):

1. **Houseflies** (they carry germs on their feet and mouth parts and settle on food).
2. **Cockroaches**.
3. **Rats and mice** (their droppings and urine).
4. **Food handlers** with dirty hands, sores or a cough.
5. **Contaminated water** (and dust and dirt carried by the air).

questions.enonce_markdown:
Outline six (6) ways of economising the cost of gas for cooking and heating in our homes.

(6 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Six ways of economising gas (1 mark each):

1. **Use a pan of the right size** and a flame that does not go beyond the base of the pan.
2. **Cover the pans with lids**, so that the food boils faster and less heat escapes.
3. **Use a pressure cooker** for foods that cook slowly, such as beans and tough meat.
4. **Cook several foods at the same time**, for example in a steamer with two or three tiers, or on one burner.
5. **Prepare everything before lighting the gas**, cut food into small pieces, and **soak dried foods** such as beans overnight, so that the cooking time is short.
6. **Turn the gas off as soon as the food is cooked** (and use the remaining heat), and keep the burners clean and check the pipes and the regulator for leaks so that no gas is wasted.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Name five (5) types of spices.

(5 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Spices** are strongly flavoured parts of plants (seeds, bark, roots, buds, fruits) that are dried and used in small quantities to give flavour and aroma to food. Five types of spices (1 mark each):

1. **Black pepper**
2. **Ginger**
3. **Nutmeg**
4. **Cloves**
5. **Cinnamon**

(Other correct examples: cardamom, turmeric, chilli and paprika.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
Complete the following abbreviations as used in nutrition.;

(i) T.V.P

(ii) H.B.V

(4 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) T.V.P = Textured Vegetable Protein.** It is a protein food made from vegetable protein (usually soya) that is processed to look and chew like meat; it is used as a meat substitute, for example by vegetarians.

**(ii) H.B.V = High Biological Value** (protein). A protein of high biological value contains **all the essential amino acids** in the amounts the body needs, so the body uses it well. Examples: meat, fish, eggs and milk.
